newsitem.title: UK: S&P cuts English China Clays CP rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P cuts English China Clays CP rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it lowered the rating on English China Clays Plc US$ 4(2) commercial paper programme to A2 from A1.
It also said it lowered English China Clays Delaware Inc.'s US$250 million 7-3/8 percent notes to A minus from A plus.
"The outlook is stable," S&P said in statement.
All rated debt is either issued or guaranteed by ECC, S&P said. The ratings have been removed from CreditWatch, where they were placed on September 16, 1996, S&P said.
"The downgrades reflect a deterioration in both the business and the financial profile of ECC, as evidenced by the group's significantly lower than expected 1996 interim results,"it said.

Operating profit in the first half of 1996 deteriorated to 12 million stg (after 18 million stg of operating exceptionals), compared with 59 million stg in the same period one year earlier, resulting in a loss of three million stg attributable to the period, S&P said.
A cash outflow in the same period resulted in net debt rising to 215 million stg at June 30, 1996, compared with 189 million stg at financial year-end 1995, S&P said.
The group is in the midst of a fundamental strategic review, which has lead to asset writedowns of 19 million stg in the first half of 1996, S&P said.
Further restructuring charges and associated cash outflows are expected as the group aims at significantly reducing its cost base.

"On the positive side, ratings continue to reflect ECC's strong industry position in its key specialty minerals business, underpinned by large market shares, a solid reserve base, high quality products, long-standing customer relations, and the group's record as a reliable supplier," S&P said.
"The group's business position, in conjunction with its solid financial posture, and historically fairly stable cash flow characteristics should stabilize ratings," S&P said.
